To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the aqueous ethanolic extract of C. sinensis (PTR‐C31911‐A) has a synergistic effect on carbapenem resistant Escherichia Coli when combined with five different antibiotics.
the combination of PTRC-31911-A with third-line antibiotics is more efficacious than monotherapy with either agent.
Camellia sinensisis an effective adjuvant to enhance the antibacterial efficacy of third‐line antibiotics against carbapenam‐resistant Esch. coli.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new combination of PTRC-31911-A and antibiotics against carbapenam-resistant Escherichia colt.
the development of an effective antibacterial combination therapy against carbapenems‐resistant E. coli.
a novel approach to improve the effectiveness of last line antibiotics by combining them with a natural product.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

PTRC‐319‐11‐A, an aquo‐ethanoleic extract of Camelliasinensis, has a synergistic effect with ertapenemen, meropenem and colistin against carbapeneme resistant Escherichia colia, which can be a potential therapeutic strategy for the treatment of carbapeneme‐resistant Escherechia colia infections.
PTRC‐319111‐A has the ability to potentiate the efficacy of last line antibiotics against carbapenam‐resistant E. coli.
PTRC‐319111‐A has a potential for synergistic antibacterial activity against carbapeneme‐resistant Esch. coli with ertapeneme, meropenem and tigecyclin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PTRC‐319‐11‐A extract has a potential to act as a synergistic enhancer of the antibacterial activity of third‐line antibiotics.
PTRC‐319‐11‐A has the potential to be a novel adjuvant in the treatment of carbapenem resistant E. coli.
the combination of PTRC-31911-A with ertapenam, meropenam, colistin tigecyclin or augmentin would prove to be more effective than monotherapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the synergistic effects of PTRC‐31811‐A and antibiotics against carbapenam resistant Escherichia colicould be a promising approach for the management of infections caused by multidrug‐resistant bacteria.
